title: Processing: Preservation and Packaging
summary: Why and how food is preserved, traditional and modern preservation methods, the functions of packaging, packaging materials, nets (developments) and environmental impact.

notes.text: Food spoils because of **micro-organisms** (bacteria, yeasts and moulds), **enzymes** in the food itself, and damage by insects and air. Preservation slows or stops spoilage so food lasts longer, can be transported and stored, and is available out of season.
Micro-organisms need **warmth**, **moisture**, **food** and usually **oxygen** to grow. Preservation methods remove one or more of these conditions.

rows: Removes water so microbes cannot grow
Biltong, dried fruit, mopane worms, dried maize
Salt draws water out of the food and microbes
High sugar concentration draws water out
Atchar, pickled onions, chakalaka in jars
Very cold stops microbe growth (does not kill them)
Heat kills microbes; sealing keeps new ones out
Dries the food and adds chemicals that slow spoilage
Useful microbes produce acid or alcohol that prevents harmful ones

notes.label: Indigenous knowledge
notes.text: Many traditional South African methods, such as drying meat into biltong, sun-drying vegetables (*imifino*) and fermenting milk into amasi, are effective preservation technologies that have been used for centuries.

items: **Protect** the product from damage, dirt, moisture and tampering.
**Preserve** it by keeping out air and microbes.
**Inform**: name, ingredients, nutrition, expiry date, barcode, instructions, recycling symbols.
**Promote** (market) the product with attractive design, colours and branding.
Make it easy to **transport, stack and display**.

rows: Strong, airtight, long shelf life, recyclable
Can dent; uses lots of energy to make
Made from oil; slow to break down; pollutes

notes.text: A **net** (development) is the flat shape that is cut out and folded to make a 3D container. A net includes **tabs** (flaps) for gluing and **fold lines** (dashed) and **cut lines** (solid). A cube's net has six squares; a cuboid box's net has six rectangles.

Too much packaging wastes resources and fills landfills. Designers can reduce the impact by using **less material**, choosing **recyclable** or **biodegradable** materials, designing for **reuse**, and printing clear recycling information.
